name: Contemplating the Lord in his manifestations (vibhūti)
method_summary: Asking how he may know the Lord while constantly contemplating him, Arjuna asks in which beings and states the Lord is to be thought of (10.17). The Lord names himself as the self in all beings and as the chief of each class of gods, seers, beings, things, sounds, times and qualities (10.20–39), and gives a rule for all else: whatever being is glorious or mighty is to be known as sprung from a portion of his splendour (10.41). Whoever knows his manifestation and yoga in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7).
notes: The text does not name this as a technique; the practice is implied by Arjuna's question (cintya, paricintayan) and the rule of 10.41.

name: Undivided devotion (ananyā bhakti)
method_summary: Devotion to the Lord alone: doing his work, holding him supreme, being devoted, free from attachment, without enmity toward any being (11.55); fixing the mind (manas) on him and worshipping him, ever yoked, with supreme faith (12.2); laying down all actions in him, holding him supreme, meditating on him with undivided yoga (12.6). By it alone the Lord can be known, seen and entered in truth (11.54); he soon delivers such devotees from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7).
signs_of_progress: the Lord is known, seen and entered in truth (11.54)
deliverance before long from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7)

name: Worship of the imperishable unmanifest (akṣara / avyakta upāsanā, BhG 12.3–5)
method_summary: Worshipping the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, constant — while restraining the whole group of the senses, being even in understanding everywhere and delighting in the welfare of all beings; such worshippers also reach the Lord (12.3–4).
prerequisites: restraint of the whole group of the senses (12.4)
delight in the welfare of all beings (12.4)

warnings.text: Greater is the hardship of those whose awareness (cetas) is attached to the unmanifest; for the unmanifest goal is reached with difficulty by the embodied.

notes: Commentators identify the object differently: Śaṅkara as brahman beyond all attributes, Rāmānuja as the individual self's own nature; the text names it only akṣara and avyakta.

name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: If one cannot hold the thought (citta) steadily fixed on the Lord, one should seek to reach him by the yoga of practice (abhyāsa-yoga) (12.9); for one incapable even of practice, work for the Lord is offered instead (12.10). In the ranking of 12.12, knowledge is better than practice. The verses do not describe the practice further.

name: Doing the Lord's work (mat-karma)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Doing the Lord's work (matkarmakṛt) is the first mark of the one who comes to him (11.55); one incapable even of the yoga of practice is to be intent on work for the Lord (matkarmaparama): even doing actions for his sake one attains perfection (12.10).

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: If unable even to work for the Lord, then, resorting to his yoga and with oneself restrained, give up the fruit of all actions (12.11); relinquishment is ranked above meditation, and peace follows it immediately (12.12).

name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Laying down all actions in the Lord, holding him supreme, worshipping him in meditation with undivided yoga; for these, whose awareness (cetas) is set on him, he becomes before long the deliverer from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.6–7).

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The wise have their thought (citta) on the Lord and their life-breaths gone into him (10.9); the most yoked fix their mind (manas) on him (12.2); 'place your mind on me alone, let your understanding enter into me; you will dwell in me thereafter' (12.8).

name: Devotional singing of the Lord's names and deeds (kīrtana, saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The devotees awaken one another and are always speaking of the Lord (kathayantaḥ), content and delighting (10.9); the world rejoices and delights in his glorification (prakīrti) (11.36).

name: Obeisance and adoration (vandana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna bows his head with joined palms (11.14), bows and prostrates (11.35), offers homage a thousand times, before, behind and on every side (11.39–40), and, prostrating his body, seeks the Lord's grace (11.44).

name: Mantra repetition (japa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of japa' (10.25): muttered recitation counted as a sacrifice and named as the Lord's manifestation among sacrifices; in the same verse the Lord is 'the one syllable' among utterances.

name: Restraint and withdrawal of the senses (indriya-saṃyama)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Those who worship the imperishable restrain the whole group of the senses (saṃniyamyendriyagrāmam) (12.4).

name: Cultivating sameness (samatva)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Being even in understanding everywhere (12.4); the same in pain and pleasure (12.13), toward enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, cold and heat (12.18), in blame and praise (12.19) — marks of the worshipper of the imperishable and of the devotee dear to the Lord.
